    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.

     9	/-!
    10	# DAT-B B-1 — the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop to `h⁰ = 1`
    11	
    12	The coverage-side normalization of the DAT-B worksheet (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md`
    13	§1.4, COV-2): on the curve bundle `Y` over a field `K` (the fibre field of the coverage
    14	argument), given an **admissible point oracle** `P` — a set of closed `K`-rational points
    15	(`residueDeg = 1`) meeting every nonempty open — and a divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with
    16	`H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`, there is an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
    17	
    18	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`
    19	  (`exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`, the keystone).
    20	
    21	The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5, worksheet §1.2 step 5) consumes this with
    22	`P :=` the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points supplied by the density oracle of B-2
    23	(`Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`); the oracle parametrization decouples the density
    24	discharge from the pure Riemann–Roch drop.
    25	
    26	## Route (worksheet §1.4, per step for the current `W'` with `h¹ = 0`, `deg = g + e'`)
    27	
    28	* **The bad locus is small** (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`): `H⁰(𝒪(W'))` is nonzero
    29	  (rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`), its base divisor
    30	  (`Scheme.baseDivisor`, the DD-F kit) has finite support consisting of closed points, so
    31	  the non-base locus contains a nonempty open (complement of a finite closed set in the
    32	  irreducible curve — it contains the generic point) and the oracle supplies an admissible
    33	  point there; the base-divisor achiever (`exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) turns
    34	  "outside the support" into an exact-order section.
    35	* **Exact drop at a rational non-base point** (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`):
    36	  `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` — sections of `W' − x` are sections of `W'`, a *proper*
    37	  submodule since the non-base section violates the deeper pole bound at `x`
    38	  (`Submodule.finrank_lt_finrank_of_lt` through the `h⁰` bridge
    39	  `finrank_divisorSections_top`) — while the χ-ledger (`chi_divisorSheaf`) with
    40	  `residueDeg x = 1` and `h¹(𝒪(W')) = 0` gives `χ(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1`; equality
    41	  forces BOTH `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` AND `h¹(𝒪(W' − x)) = 0` — the induction
    42	  invariant.
    43	* **Terminate at `e' = 0`**: `h⁰ = 1` by the rank anchor at `deg = g`, `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`.
    44	
    45	The strict-drop precedents `h0_normalization_sub_single_lt` (`PFib.lean`) and
    46	`h0_window_sub_single_lt` (`CarveDegreePinch.lean`) are window-specific mirrors of the
    47	drop step (worksheet risk 3 mitigation); their `deg_single`/`coeffAt` bookkeeping is
    48	imitated, not consumed.  Pure field level — no scheme beyond the fibre curve appears
    49	(the DD-F discipline).  The genus enters only through `hχ : χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g`; the
    50	worksheet's standing `h⁰(𝒪_Y) = 1` is not needed by this brick and is not threaded.
    51	-/
    52	
    53	set_option autoImplicit false
    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    58	
    59	attribute [local instance] AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
    60	  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.overModule
    61	
    62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    63	
    64	open Scheme
    65	
    66	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    67	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    68	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    69	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    70	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    71	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    72	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    73	
    74	/-! ## The bad locus is small: an admissible non-base point -/
    75	
    76	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    77	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
    78	/-- **An admissible non-base point** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 1): if `H⁰(𝒪(W))` is nonzero
    79	and `P` is dense (meets every nonempty open) and consists of closed points, then some
    80	`x ∈ P` is *not* a base point of the system: some nonzero section `f ∈ H⁰(𝒪(W))` has
    81	exact order at `x`, `(W + div f)ₓ = 0`.  The base locus is contained in the support of
    82	the base divisor `bd(H⁰(𝒪(W)))` — a finite set of closed points, whose complement is a
    83	nonempty open (it contains the generic point); the base-divisor achiever
    84	(`Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
    85	outside the support. -/
    86	theorem exists_admissible_nonbase_point (P : Set Y)
    87	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
    88	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
    89	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W)) :
    90	    ∃ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (_ : x ∈ P) (f : Y.functionField)
    91	      (_ : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0),
    92	      coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
    93	        = 0 := by
    94	  classical
    95	  set T : Submodule K Y.functionField := divisorSections K W ⊤ with hT
    96	  have hTne : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0 := by
    97	    refine Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot (fun hbot => ?_)
    98	    have hfr : Module.finrank K ↥T = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) :=
    99	      finrank_divisorSections_top K W
   100	    rw [hbot, finrank_bot] at hfr
   101	    omega
   102	  set B : Y.CurveDivisor := Scheme.baseDivisor K T W hTne with hB
   103	  -- the support of the base divisor is a finite set of closed points
   104	  have hclosed : IsClosed (⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y)) :=
   105	    isClosed_biUnion_finset (fun p _ =>
   106	      isClosed_singleton_of_ne_genericPoint (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) p.2)
   107	  set U : Y.Opens :=
   108	    ⟨(⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y))ᶜ, hclosed.isOpen_compl⟩ with hU
   109	  have hUne : (U : Set Y).Nonempty := by
   110	    refine ⟨genericPoint Y, fun hmem => ?_⟩
   111	    obtain ⟨p, _, hp⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp hmem
   112	    exact p.2 (Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hp).symm
   113	  obtain ⟨x, hxP, hxU⟩ := hdense U hUne
   114	  have hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y := hPcl x hxP
   115	  -- outside the support the base multiplicity vanishes
   116	  have hxc : x ∉ ⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y) := hxU
   117	  have hxB : coeffAt hx B = 0 := by
   118	    by_contra hne
   119	    exact hxc (Set.mem_iUnion₂.mpr
   120	      ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mpr hne, rfl⟩)
   121	  have hBat : (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T W ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) = 0 := by
   122	    rw [← Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hTne hx]
   123	    exact hxB
   124	  -- the achiever realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
   125	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf, hach⟩ :=
   126	    Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt K (le_refl T) hTne hx
   127	  exact ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfT, hf, hach.trans hBat⟩
   128	
   129	/-! ## The exact drop at a rational non-base point -/
   130	
   131	/-- **The exact drop** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 2): at a closed `K`-rational point `x`
   132	(`residueDeg x = 1`) that is not a base point of `H⁰(𝒪(W))` — witnessed by a nonzero
   133	section `f` of exact order at `x` — and under `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`,
   134	
   135	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − x)) + 1 = h⁰(𝒪(W))`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − x)) = 0`.
   136	
   137	`≤`: sections of `W − x` are sections of `W` vanishing one order deeper at `x`, a proper
   138	subspace since `f` violates the deeper bound — one linear condition as `residueDeg x = 1`.
   139	`≥`: the χ-ledger gives `χ(𝒪(W − x)) = χ(𝒪(W)) − 1 = h⁰(𝒪(W)) − 1` and `h¹ ≥ 0`.
   140	Equality forces both conclusions — the induction invariant of the greedy drop. -/
   141	theorem h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase (W : Y.CurveDivisor)
   142	    (h1W : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1))
   143	    {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (hdx : Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   144	    {f : Y.functionField} (hfW : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0)
   145	    (hnb : coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
   146	      = 0) :
   147	    Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + 1
   148	        = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) ∧
   149	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
   150	  -- sections of `W − x` sit inside sections of `W` …
   151	  have hle : divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤
   152	      ≤ divisorSections K W ⊤ := by
   153	    refine divisorSections_mono K ?_ ⊤
   154	    refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   155	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub]
   156	    by_cases hyx : y = x
   157	    · subst hyx
   158	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   159	      omega
   160	    · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   161	      omega
   162	  -- … properly: the exact-order section violates the deeper bound at `x`
   163	  have hfnot : f ∉ divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤ := by
   164	    intro hmem
   165	    have h0le := (mem_divisorSections_top_iff K hf).mp hmem
   166	    have hcoeff := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp h0le x hx
   167	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub,
   168	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self] at hcoeff
   169	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hnb
   170	    omega
   171	  have hne : divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤
   172	      ≠ divisorSections K W ⊤ := by
   173	    intro heq
   174	    rw [← heq] at hfW
   175	    exact hfnot hfW
   176	  have hdrop : Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
   177	      < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) := by
   178	    have hlt := Submodule.finrank_lt_finrank_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_ne hle hne)
   179	    rwa [finrank_divisorSections_top K _, finrank_divisorSections_top K _] at hlt
   180	  -- the χ-ledger on both levels
   181	  have hchiW := chi_divisorSheaf K W
   182	  have hchiWx := chi_divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   183	  have hdegsub : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   184	      = CurveDivisor.deg K W - 1 := by
   185	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1, hdx,
   186	      Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
   187	  rw [hdegsub] at hchiWx
   188	  have hh0W : Sheaf.chi (Y.divisorSheaf K W) = (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) : ℤ) :=
   189	    Sheaf.chi_eq_h0 h1W
   190	  have hchidef : Sheaf.chi (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
   191	      = (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ)
   192	        - (Sheaf.h1 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := rfl
   193	  have hh1 : Sheaf.h1 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) = 0 := by omega
   194	  refine ⟨by omega, ?_⟩
   195	  haveI := moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   196	  exact Module.finrank_zero_iff.mp hh1
   197	
   198	/-! ## The keystone: the greedy drop to `h⁰ = 1` -/
   199	
   200	/-- **COV-2, the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop** (★ B-1 keystone, worksheet §1.4):
   201	on the curve bundle `Y` over the field `K` with `χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g`, let `P` be an
   202	admissible point oracle — closed points, `K`-rational (`residueDeg = 1`), dense (meeting
   203	every nonempty open).  Then every divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`
   204	admits an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
   205	
   206	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`.
   207	
   208	Induction on `e`: at each step the rank anchor gives `h⁰ = e' + 1 ≥ 1`, the oracle
   209	supplies a rational non-base point (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`), and the exact
   210	drop (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`) preserves the invariant `h¹ = 0` while
   211	lowering the degree budget by one.  The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5) instantiates
   212	`P` with the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points of B-2. -/
   213	theorem exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (g : ℕ)
   214	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   215	    (P : Set Y)
   216	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
   217	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
   218	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   219	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (e : ℕ)
   220	    (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e)
   221	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1)) :
   222	    ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   223	      (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   224	      Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   225	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) := by
   226	  suffices H : ∀ (e : ℕ) (W : Y.CurveDivisor),
   227	      CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e →
   228	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) →
   229	      ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   230	        (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   231	        Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   232	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) from
   233	    H e W hdeg h1
   234	  intro e
   235	  induction e with
   236	  | zero =>
   237	    intro W hdeg h1
   238	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   239	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   240	    refine ⟨0, le_refl 0, by rw [CurveDivisor.deg_zero, Nat.cast_zero], ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   241	    · intro x hx hne
   242	      exact (hne (CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero hx)).elim
   243	    · rw [sub_zero]
   244	      push_cast at hanchor
   245	      omega
   246	    · rw [sub_zero]
   247	      exact h1
   248	  | succ e ih =>
   249	    intro W hdeg h1
   250	    -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) = e + 2 > 0` by the rank anchor
   251	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   252	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   253	    have hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) := by
   254	      push_cast at hanchor
   255	      omega
   256	    -- an admissible non-base point and the exact drop there
   257	    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfW, hf, hnb⟩ :=
   258	      exists_admissible_nonbase_point P hdense hPcl W hpos
   259	    obtain ⟨hdrop, h1'⟩ :=
   260	      h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase W h1 hx (hPdeg x hxP) hfW hf hnb
   261	    have hdeg' : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) = (g : ℤ) + e := by
   262	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   263	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one, hdeg]
   264	      push_cast
   265	      ring
   266	    obtain ⟨S', hS'0, hS'deg, hS'P, hS'h0, hS'h1⟩ :=
   267	      ih (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) hdeg' h1'
   268	    have hsplit : W - (S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   269	        = W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - S' := by
   270	      abel
   271	    refine ⟨S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   272	    · -- effectivity
   273	      refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   274	      have h0S' := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp hS'0 y hy
   275	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at h0S'
   276	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
   277	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   278	      · subst hyx
   279	        rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   280	        omega
   281	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   282	        omega
   283	    · -- degree
   284	      rw [CurveDivisor.deg_add, hS'deg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   285	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
   286	      push_cast
   287	      ring
   288	    · -- support in `P`
   289	      intro y hy hne
   290	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hne
   291	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   292	      · subst hyx
   293	        exact hxP
   294	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx, add_zero] at hne
   295	        exact hS'P y hy hne
   296	    · rw [hsplit]
   297	      exact hS'h0
   298	    · rw [hsplit]
   299	      exact hS'h1
   300	
   301	end AlgebraicGeometry

     1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.

     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartTwistSplit
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.DegreeBaseFieldInvariance
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# COV-1 input 2: the DEGREE of the presenting class of the twisted fibre class
    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean` names the Čech class that presents the twisted fibre class
    13	over the splitting field `L`:
    14	
    15	  `M₀ · CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z)`.
    16	
    17	`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 2–4 then need its `L`-degree, because that is what decides whether the
    18	class can carry an effective witness with `h¹ = 0` at all: the greedy drop of
    19	`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean` consumes a divisor of degree `g + e`.
    20	
    21	This file computes it, and the computation is exactly the degree ledger the worksheet pins:
    22	
    23	  `classDeg L (presenting class) = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`   when `λ` is degree-zero,
    24	
    25	so under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g` it is `+g` — and with the drop budget
    26	`e` folded in (`deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g − e`) it is `g + e`, which is `exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`'s
    27	hypothesis on the nose.
    28	
    29	## The two halves, and which one is nontrivial
    30	
    31	* the **twist factor** is a base class base-changed to `L`, so its `L`-degree is its
    32	  `k`-degree by **E-iv-alg** (`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`) — no per-field
    33	  ledger constant crosses, which is the I-0204 discipline;
    34	* the **`λ` factor** has `L`-degree zero, and this is where degree-zero-ness is *spent*.
    35	  It is `degAt λ (testPoint) = 0` read through the degree seam: `degAt` of a class whose
    36	  affine collapse is a plus unit of `relPicMk M₀` is `classDeg` of `M₀`
    37	  (`degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk`).
    38	
    39	The second half is the reason this file exists rather than being three `rw`s inside COV-1: the
    40	seam from "`μ` is presented over `L` by `M₀`" to "`classDeg L M₀ = degAt μ`" is a statement
    41	about `PicEtAff.map` versus `picEtMap`, not about degrees.
    42	
    43	## Main declarations
    44	
    45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_cechPicMap_base_of_field` — the `L`-degree of a base class
    46	  base-changed to `L` is its `k`-degree (E-iv-alg in the `relCurveMap` spelling).
    47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange` — the twist factor contributes
    48	  exactly `m·d₁ − deg_k Z`.
    49	-/
    50	
    51	set_option autoImplicit false
    52	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
    53	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    54	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
    55	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    56	
    57	universe u
    58	
    59	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    60	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
    61	
    62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    63	
    64	open AlgebraicJacobian
    65	
    66	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    67	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    68	
    69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
    71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    72	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    73	
    74	noncomputable section
    75	
    76	/-! ## E-iv-alg in the `relCurveMap` spelling -/
    77	
    78	variable (C) in
    79	/-- **The degree of a base class is base-field invariant** — E-iv-alg
    80	(`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`) read along `relCurveMap C k L` rather than along
    81	the raw whisker.  The two agree by `relCurveMap_eq_overSpecMap_ofId`, and this is the spelling
    82	every chart-layer statement uses. -/
    83	theorem classDeg_cechPicMap_base_of_field (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    84	    (Λ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic) :
    85	    classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left) Λ)
    86	      = classDeg k Λ :=
    87	  classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C (Algebra.ofId k L) Λ
    88	
    89	variable (C) in
    90	/-- **The twist factor's contribution to the degree**: `m·d₁ − deg_k Z`, computed at the
    91	splitting field but equal to a `k`-level quantity — the point of routing it through E-iv-alg
    92	rather than through a per-field ledger. -/
    93	theorem classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] (m : ℕ)
    94	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
    95	    classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left)
    96	        (chartTwistClass C m Z))
    97	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
    98	  rw [classDeg_cechPicMap_base_of_field C L]
    99	  change classDeg k (thetaCechClass C ^ m * (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass k Z)⁻¹) = _
   100	  rw [classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, classDeg_pow, classDeg_picClass]
   101	  ring
   102	
   103	/-! ## Where degree-zero-ness is spent: the `λ` factor -/
   104	
   105	variable (C) in
   106	/-- **The presenting class's `classDeg` equals the transported plus-class degree.**
   107	
   108	`classDeg L M = degAff L (PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν))`, whenever `M` presents
   109	`ν` over `L`.  Read the statement, not the ambition: the right-hand side is the plus-class
   110	degree **at `L`**, and this is `degAff_unit` plus `relPicDeg_relPicMk`, nothing more.
   111	
   112	**A CORRECTION, and it is the reason this docstring is now shorter than it was** (issue I-0614,
   113	found by fresh-context review).  The previous version claimed this theorem was the `w4-datb`
   114	§1.2 step-2 seam — that it carried `degAt ν = 0` over to `classDeg M = 0` — and justified the
   115	`K → L` step by citing `degAff_map_eq`.  **No such lemma exists**: the only occurrence of that
   116	name in the workspace was that docstring.  So the claim was a phantom citation, and the step it
   117	claimed to make is genuinely absent:
   118	
   119	* what the coverage argument HAS is `degAt ν t = degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)`, at `K`;
   120	* what this theorem's RHS mentions is `degAff L (PicEtAff.map C L …)`, at `L`;
   121	* nothing in the tree equates them.  The missing brick is **base-field invariance of `degAff`
   122	  under `PicEtAff.map`**, a small real lemma shaped like the landed `degAff_baseFieldShuffle`
   123	  (`Picard/Pic0ThetaAssembly.lean:67`) — measured, not guessed: `exact?` on
   124	  `degAff L (map C L a) = degAff K a` finds nothing.
   125	
   126	**STEP 2 IS NOW DISCHARGED (2026-07-28), and this paragraph's "NOT discharged" is superseded.**
   127	The missing `degAff` invariance was proved as `PicEtAff.degAff_map`
   128	(`Picard/DegreeZeroBaseField.lean`) — and it needs *no* hypothesis on `L/K` at all, not even
   129	finiteness, so it is weaker-premised than the `degAff_baseFieldShuffle` shape predicted above.
   130	Step 2 itself is `classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff` / `classDeg_presenting_eq_zero`
   131	(`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`), which reaches `classDeg L M = degAff K a`
   132	directly and therefore does **not** route through this theorem.
   133	
   134	This theorem is kept because it is true and was the first half of the seam, but it remains
   135	without consumers: the landed route reads the `K`-side degree rather than the `L`-side one, so
   136	its `PicEtAff.map`-shaped right-hand side is no longer the useful spelling.
   137	
   138	The other half of the ledger — the twist factor's contribution — IS complete
   139	(`classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange` above, via E-iv-alg). -/
   140	theorem classDeg_of_presenting {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   141	    (ν : picEt C (overSpec k K)) {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L]
   142	    [IsScalarTower k K L] (M : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CechPic)
   143	    (hM : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)
   144	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)) :
   145	    classDeg L M = PicEtAff.degAff L (PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)) := by
   146	  rw [hM, PicEtAff.degAff_unit, relPicDeg_relPicMk]
   147	
   148	end
   149	
   150	end AlgebraicGeometry

   200	**This RETRACTS the "no positional introduction rule exists" record** of
   201	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s closing note and of the memory item filed with it.  That
   202	record was measured, and its measurement was right about what it tested — five variants, all
   203	timing out at 1000000+ heartbeats:
   204	
   205	* `exact`/`refine` with all twelve components as ONE anonymous constructor;
   206	* the witness clause pre-bundled as a `have`;
   207	* either curve spelling normalised to the other;
   208	* `(isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness …).mpr` applied to the twelve-tuple;
   209	* the trivial splitting `L := K`.

   211	What none of them tested is **staging the existentials**.  Introducing them one at a time —
   212	eight `Exists.intro`s and a four-component tail — costs nothing at the DEFAULT 200000
   213	heartbeat budget.  The diagnosis the old record gives is still correct: the anonymous
   214	constructor makes Lean unify the seven instance slots *while `L` is still a metavariable*,
   215	re-checking `(relCurve C L).CechPic` against `((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor` on each
   216	attempted assignment.  Staging fixes `L` at the first step, so every later component is
   217	checked against a closed type and the two spellings never race.
   218	
   219	**The transferable rule**, and it is stronger than the one it replaces: for a deep existential
   220	over types-with-instances, `refine Exists.intro x ?_` repeatedly, rather than one tuple.  The
   221	old advice ("restate the definition with one spelling") would have been a large refactor of a

   224	theorem isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness
   225	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (ν : picEt C (overSpec k K))
   226	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]

   235	  refine Exists.intro L ?_
   236	  refine Exists.intro ‹Field L› ?_
   237	  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra k L› ?_
   238	  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra K L› ?_
   239	  refine Exists.intro ‹IsScalarTower k K L› ?_
   240	  refine Exists.intro ‹Module.Finite K L› ?_
   241	  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra.IsSeparable K L› ?_

   244	
   245	variable (C) in
   246	/-- **The TRIVIAL splitting `L := K`** — the variant the predecessor record singled out as
   247	"worth wanting" and reported as unelaborable.
   248	
   249	At a field where the class is *already* honest, no extension is needed: a witness divisor over

   260	theorem isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self
   261	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (ν : picEt C (overSpec k K))
   262	    (M : (relCurve C K).CechPic)
   263	    (hM : PicEtAff.map C K (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)
   264	      = PicEtAff.unit C K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M))

   271	variable (C) in
   272	/-- **COV-1's introduction rule for `chartLocus` membership.**

   276	* a divisor `W` on `C_L` whose class is `M₀ · (twist class base-changed to L)` and whose
   277	  `H¹` vanishes,
   278

     8	/-!
     9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
    12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
    13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
    14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
    15	index per point of `T`".
    16	
    17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
    18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
    19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
    20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
    21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
    22	connection is what this file supplies.
    23	
    24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
    25	
    26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
    27	
    28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
    29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
    30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
    31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
    32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
    33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
    34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
    35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
    36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
    37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
    38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
    39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
    40	
    41	## Main declarations
    42	
    43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
    44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
    45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
    47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
    48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
    49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
    50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
    51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
    53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
    54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
    55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
    56	-/

    58	set_option autoImplicit false
    59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    61	universe u
    62	
    63	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    64	
    65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    66	
    67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    70	
    71	noncomputable section
    72	
    73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
    74	
    75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
    76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
    77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
    78	
    79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
    80	
    81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
    82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
    83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
    84	
    85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
    86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
    87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
    88	
    89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
    90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
    91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
    92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
    96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
    98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
    99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
   100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
   101	
   102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
   103	
   104	variable (C) in
   105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
   106	
   107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
   108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
   109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
   110	
   111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
   112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
   113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
   114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
   115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
   116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
   117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
   118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
   119	
   120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
   121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
   122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
   123	
   124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
   125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
   126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
   127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
   128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   134	  intro T s
   135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
   136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
   137	
   138	variable (C) in
   139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
   140	
   141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
   142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
   143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
   144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
   145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
   152	
   153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
   154	
   155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
   156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
   157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
   158	
   159	variable (C) in
   160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
   161	
   162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
   163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
   164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
   165	
   166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
   167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
   168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
   169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
   170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
   171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
   172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
   173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
   176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
   178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
   179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
   180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
   181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
   182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
   183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
   184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
   185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
   186	
   187	end

   189	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	/-!
    11	# Legal chart indices after finite base change
    12	
    13	This file supplies the positive replacement for a base-field genus divisor-degree assumption.
    14	Every challenge curve has a closed point; its residue field is a finite extension over which the
    15	curve has a rational point.  More strongly, a point over a separable closure spreads through the
    16	cofiltered limit of finite subextensions, producing a point over a finite separable extension.
    17	The graph of either point then produces a legal chart index at every natural parameter, in
    18	particular at the genus.  The stronger construction matters over imperfect fields: an arbitrary
    19	closed point can be inseparable even though smoothness guarantees that a separable one can be
    20	chosen.
    21	
    22	## Main declarations
    23	
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_point` — every challenge curve acquires a point over a
    25	  finite extension, obtained from a closed point and its residue field.
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteSubextension_point_of_point` — a point over an algebraic
    27	  extension of a finitely presented scheme spreads to one finite subextension.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_separable_point` — every challenge curve acquires a point
    29	  over a finite separable extension, with no point or divisor-degree hypothesis.
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_galois_point` — normal closure upgrades this to a finite
    31	  Galois extension, still without a new curve hypothesis.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangePoint` — the fibre-product lift of an extension-valued point to
    33	  a rational point of the base-changed curve.
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpecFieldExtension_mem_fpqcTopology` — a field extension is an fpqc
    35	  singleton cover of the base field.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fpqc_pointCover` — one finite fpqc cover carrying a point of the
    37	  curve.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fpqc_chartIndices` — that same cover supports a legal chart index
    39	  at every natural parameter.
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_galois_chartIndices` — the common cover can be chosen finite
    41	  Galois, in the form consumed by Galois descent.
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fpqc_chartIndex` — the finite cover and a legal chart index are
    43	  produced together.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_chartIndex` — every natural parameter has a legal
    45	  chart index after one finite base change.
    46	-/

   137	  rw [CommRingCat.hom_ofHom, RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff]

   151	/-- Every challenge curve has a point on one finite fpqc cover of the base field. -/
   152	theorem exists_fpqc_pointCover :
   153	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
